As I was working in the staff, the body for personnel required each member to give his particulars, so there were people who were working in the staff already, and on the basis of applications by former JNA members, they were engaged as members of the staff. Then there were certain members who had not been members of the JNA, but they were employed by the staff because the members of the former staff of Serb ethnic origin abandoned the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like the witness to be shown a document and may it first be marked for identification, please? I have a sufficient number of copies for the court and for the Prosecutor. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D165/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise -- we had only one copy with two persons. It consists of a letter and five annexes, so will you please take into consideration this correction, because I have the full number of pages with me here, so all the others may not be complete. Mr. Kevric, will you please look at this document? Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am familiar with the contents of this document. It was never given to me, but I know that it was sent, because this information was required. I can also recognise Enes Pajic, who was responsible for personnel in the staff. He is still a member of the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you find on these lists your own name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my name is number 1 on the list of active military personnel working in the municipal TO staff of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, can you confirm in this court that you personally know that all these persons, at the time indicated by the date when the list was compiled, were in fact working in the TO staff as indicated in these lists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I know all these persons and the posts they held at the time are indicated and their qualifications are also indicated, with the exception of, in the last part, Halilic, an active military person -- he was killed during the war and he was an officer in the quartermaster department, working with me in the logistics department.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, since these are lists of members of TO staff on this date as indicated on the list, that is, the end of April, and in view of the fact that this witness has confirmed the truthfulness of the contents and as this is a relevant document, I tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may tender it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric, this list, as you have said, does not include Zejnil Delalic, because he was not a member of the TO staff, as you have said. But I have another question to put to you. As you were a member of the TO staff, or, rather, of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina throughout 1992, can you tell the court whether Mr. Delalic was at any time the commander of the municipal Territorial Defence staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic was never performing the duties of commander of the municipal TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, did Mr. Zejnil Delalic at any point in time in the course of 1992 -- was he a member of the staff of the Territorial Defence of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic was never a member of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, are you familiar with the composition of your staff and its structure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am familiar with the structure of the TO staff. I am familiar with all the persons who were working in the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask the witness to be shown a chart from the third volume of the expert witness document, V-D/5. I have it here in Bosnian in a sufficient number of copies, but I think it may be shown to the court and the witness on the ELMO as well as the chart in English, which is included in the folder. (Handed). Could the English version be placed on the ELMO and could the witness be given the Bosnian version? I cannot see it on the ELMO. We do not have it on the monitor. Can we see the chart in English on the ELMO, please? Mr. Kevric, when pointing to anything, will you please move it so that the court can see it and all the other participants in the hearing? First, may I ask you whether you recognise what this chart means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a diagram of the structure of the staff. Heading the staff is the commander of the municipal staff of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before beginning any explanations, do you personally figure here as a person serving in a particular area on this chart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am here as a logistics body.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you indicate what part of it that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The rear -- it is this part (witness indicates).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was your rear agency a developed structure, did it have services, officers in charge of those services and the like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The rear agency was developed and all the services were represented from the quartermasters, transportation service, technical, medical, building construction, financial -- all of these services had one or two officers working there. Here we have the supply service, traffic service and technical service and these are indicated on the chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who were the commanders of the municipal TO Defence staff in the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the staff of the Territorial Defence of Konjic was first Redzepovic, then Esad Ramic, then Omer Boric, also Catic Mirsad, and after that, Enver Tahirovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm, Mr. Kevric, that this is a truthful diagram of the structure of the Territorial Defence staff, all the staff of the armed forces of Konjic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I confirm that this organisational chart is indeed correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the witness is a part of the staff represented on this diagram and that he confirmed the truthfulness of the same, I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is the number D145/1, annex 5D, 5/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric -- no, let me rephrase that question -- which were the defence forces of Konjic at the time, in addition to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from the Territorial Defence, there were HVO units and there was the MUP of the Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When taking over military facilities in the first 10 days of May, did the HVO participate with you -- both the HVO and the MUP -- in those operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Initially, as I have already said, participating were HVO units and reserve units of the police -- the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, do you know whether, in that period, that is, the first 10 days of May 1992, were there any attempts for the control and command over TO and HVO units to be united, and was some kind of a joint body set up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- yes, for the operations to be prepared properly and for the town of Konjic to be defended, the representatives of the TO staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina insisted on the formation of joint commands and a joint command was indeed formed on 12 May and after a session of the war presidency, that joint command was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, would it be convenient for us to break now before I go on to another area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think so. We can break now. We will reassemble at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please remind the witness he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, Sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness requested of me, and I would like to suggest that we all try to speak a little bit louder, and also the witness had some damage in his ears as a consequence of war, so if we could turn up the volume -- if I can ask the technical booth if we can turn it up so that my microphone could be put on louder and also especially what the interpreters are saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: My understanding of this equipment is that you can increase your own volume -- each one can increase their own volume.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric -- your Honours, may I proceed the court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the break, Mr. Kevric, if you will recall, we were talking about the establishment of the joint command. Can you please tell me whether you personally were a member of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the joint command. I was on duty as an assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the structure of the joint command during the period when it was operational?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the structure of the joint command and I can also explain it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask the questions. Can you please tell me who was the commander of the joint command and who was his deputy, that is, who was his chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the joint command was Mr. Esad Ramic and his deputy was Mr. Zebic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning, was another person the commander of the joint command -- that is, not at the very beginning but during an initial period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at first the commander was Omer Boric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what were Esad Ramic and Omer Boric -- what positions did they hold in the staff of the Territorial Defence before they moved to these positions in the joint command? Did you understand my question? What duties did Omer Boric and Esad Ramic have in the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not give you precise answers to that. I know that Esad Ramic was the commander of the staff of the Territorial Defence, but I know that at one point he was an operations officer. When Ramic was in operations, then I know that Omer Boric was the commander of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. I would now like to show the witness a chart of the structure of the joint command. I have enough copies both in Bosnian and English. I would like them distributed to the Trial Chamber and everybody else. (Handed). . Mr. Kevric, would you please look at this chart carefully and then I will ask you, when I ask questions of you regarding the chart, that you look at the ELMO and that you use the pointer in order to show me the appropriate duties that I will be asking you about. Can you tell me, in the upper rectangle where you have commander of the joint command you have two names, Esad Ramic and Omer Boric. Can you tell me, did these people -- these two persons relieve each other as commanders of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether, during the period when Omer Boric and Esad Ramic were commanders of the joint command, that is, in both those periods, was the same chief of staff on duty and is that also marked in the appropriate rectangle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout the period of this relevant time, Dinko Zebic was the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the role of Dinko Zebic in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dinko Zebic was on duty as commander of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show me, what was your place in this particular organisational scheme that you occupied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness indicates).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, within your department, that is, within your section of the joint command, were there other services involved which are represented on this chart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in this chart several services were indicated. The medical, traffic, construction services are also indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, is this a truthful representation which shows that both the members of the HVO and the TO were equally represented in the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a truthful representation and it is truthful in terms of representation of both the HVO and the TO members.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, during which period did this joint command function as it is presented here on this chart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This joint command functioned up until the preparation for the operations at Borci.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, was Mr. Zejnil Delalic at any time commander of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic was at no time commander of the joint command, nor was he a member of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Zejnil Delalic during this period at any time a superior officer in terms of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Zejnil Delalic was never a superior person to the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, since this witness authenticated this chart, since he was a part of the structure displayed here and since this is a relevant chart, I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can tender it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This chart has been admitted under the number that it was marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Defence Exhibit D166/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric, did you have a relationship of cooperation with the HVO and MUP, even at the time when there was no joint command between the TO and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did have a relationship of cooperation, that is, during the initial operations during the take-over of the Ljuta barracks and the facility at Zlatar and what I stated at the beginning -- the take-over of the Celebici barracks, which was only with the members of MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the Konjic HVO accepting the unity of command and the supreme command of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the HVO did not accept the superiority of the TO staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who, during 1992, was the superior structure over the units, that is, the staff of the Konjic HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The staff that was superior to the Konjic HVO staff was the staff in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, who was the superior body to the station of public security in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Ministry of Internal Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina was superior to the station of public security in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which was your superior command, that is, either the staff or the command which was superior to the municipal staff in Konjic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, the staff of TO in Bosnia-Herzegovina was superior to the municipal staff TO -- until 17 November of that year, when the 4th Corps was formed and, from then on, the TO staff in Konjic is subordinate to the 4th Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the establishment of the joint command, were certain joint combat operations prepared and then implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were some joint combat operations which were carried out in the area of Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the TO staff, do you know who issued, that is, who was signing the orders for combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The orders for combat operations were signed jointly. The commander of the joint command and the chief of staff would sign them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness now please be shown a document which has been marked in the third volume of the expert material and which had been admitted into evidence, so that I could ask certain questions. I have enough copies for the Chamber and for my colleagues and for the Prosecution. (Handed). Mr. Kevric, would you please look at this order? Please, if the document has already been marked, would you tell me its number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document has been already marked. It is D145/1, annex 5D, 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric, have you had a chance to look through this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this document issued on 25 May 1992 at the time when the joint command was functioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: 27 May, not 25 May.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, 27 May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this document was issued at a time when the joint command was functioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether this was a usual way in which documents, that is, orders, were signed by the joint command, that is, the documents that were issued by the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the usual way in which all documents were signed when there was agreement about mutual participation in combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, do you personally know of this joint order which was issued on 27 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand your question very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you personally know of the existence of this order that you are now holding in your hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received this order, because I had to support these units in the event that they needed logistic support.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, are you personally familiar with who was the responsible commander in the combat operations for the preparation of units, the course and outcome of the combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The person responsible for combat operations was Mr. Zvonko Zovko who was in command of the unit, who was situated on Mount Preslica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this exhibit has already been admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit, the witness has just confirmed the truth of its contents. May it now be returned into the record? Mr. Kevric, do you know whether, after the Operation Donje Selo, military weapons were found and seized from the inhabitants of that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, weapons were found on the inhabitants of Donje Selo and the technical service that was assigned to collect those weapons took over the weapons found from the military police commander, Pijo Luicevic, the police of the HVO. On that occasion up-to-date weaponry was found, machine-guns, M80 of the latest date, with a folding butt used by units of the former Yugoslav People's Army, that is, by armoured units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the technical service that collected those weapons come under your authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The technical service was under my control and it was the service that collected and registered the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric, will you tell me, please, whether, after the battles for the liberation of Bradina, weapons were found, captured and collected from the persons who participated in the fighting at Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, weapons were found among the inhabitants of Bradina. Some of those weapons were immediately issued to units participating in the combat operations and a smaller share was taken to the Celebici barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was held at the Celebici barracks where the weapons were placed -- you referred to the Celebici barracks just now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Celebici barracks, there was an underground facility, which was used to store fuel in barrels and, as this was the safest facility protected from the air force, we had that facility to store the weapons there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric, you said that orders on which agreement was reached were signed by the commander of the TO and the commander of the HVO. Will you tell me, please, regarding the appointments made by the joint command, who would sign those appointments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Appointments to positions in the formations by the joint command would be signed by the commander and the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally, at that time, when you were appointed assistant commander for logistics -- did you have an appointment signed in that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had an appointment that was signed in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Zejnil Delalic, as far as you know, ever sign any appointment that was signed by the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. Zejnil Delalic never signed an appointment, because he was not a member of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, do you know whether the war presidency of Konjic municipality appointed Zejnil Delalic as coordinator between the war presidency and the defence forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. The war presidency did appoint Mr. Zejnil Delalic in the second half of May. I really could not tell you the exact date, whether it was the 19th or the 18th -- I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what activities Mr. Delalic predominantly engaged in while holding this position of coordinator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic mainly engaged in logistic matters -- supplies of materiel, equipment, food, communications equipment. Also, Mr. Zejnil Delalic was active in the project of setting in motion a mini railway from Konjic to Jablanica and, later on, from Konjic to Tarcin. He was also involved in the transportation of a vast number of refugees arriving in Konjic from eastern Bosnia and eastern Herzegovina. He was also active as a coordinator in linking up the electricity grid.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, let me ask you, in view of these activities that you have described and the work that you yourself performed, did you personally have occasional or frequent contacts with Mr. Delalic regarding his activities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because of my very considerable responsibilities at the time, ranging from the organisation of the army, or, rather, the logistic body, and logistic units which had to carry out tasks assigned to them, I would occasionally have contact with Mr. Zejnil Delalic, but I authorised my heads of services and especially the head of the technical transportation and building construction service to be able to contact Mr. Zejnil Delalic and, on several occasions, I was officially absent from the town of Konjic, so I was away looking for materiel and other equipment from other units and other staffs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, in view of the fact that you had such a difficult task to perform, that is, while fighting was going on, to try to find the resources required for life and for combat, tell me whether the TO staff had several requests for logistic support from the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The TO staff really did receive a vast number of requests, starting from requirements in terms of food stuffs, containers for the transportation of food, blankets, communication equipment, and other technical supplies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the war presidency have the legal duty to provide logistic support for the defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war presidency of Konjic municipality was obliged, by law, to provide what I have already listed, because we, as the TO staff, did not have any reserves, nor the possibility of receiving regular supplies from the Bosnia-Herzegovina TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of these numerous requests and very limited possibilities, did the need arise for coordinating views and coming to an agreement that would then be addressed to the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a need for coordination, especially when planning combat operations so as to convey to the war presidency the real needs, because, under those conditions, the war presidency had to be very economical and in order to avoid members of the army contacting the war presidency directly, the coordinator would occasionally attend when such logistic problems were discussed and would inform the war presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, did Mr. Zejnil Delalic, as a coordinator -- was Mr. Zejnil Delalic at any point in time a person of superior authority in relation to you, or the TO staff, or the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Zejnil Delalic was never a superior for me -- I had my own staff commander and the joint command. I received orders only from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In those agreements regarding your logistic needs and the coordination of those needs, do you know, or did you ever see the coordinator signing any such document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see it, mostly documents when the meeting was attended by the coordinator in connection with those logistic needs. In the interests of expediency while the army was being set up and in order to provide logistic support as quickly as possible, Mr. Zejnil Delalic would attend as a witness so as to be able to convey the information to the war presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown two documents which the Prosecutor has had marked as his own exhibits? I do not have the numbers, but I have sufficient copies for the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution, and these are documents dated 6 June and 8 June. (Handed). I think the number is P211 -- I am not sure about the other one. The documents have already been marked for identification by the Prosecution. I am not going to tender them into evidence by the Defence; I just have a question to put to the witness in connection with these documents. Could you please tell me under what number they have been marked?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The order dated 8 June 1992 is D167/1 and the order number 1/5, 92. The other order number 1/4, 92 is D168/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, will you please look at this document dated 6 June called "organisational order"? Tell me, please, does an order of this kind have anything to do with the affairs you were engaged in, that is, logistics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this kind of order is related to logistic activities, because we did not have in our possession a sufficient number of motor vehicles which could be used for the transportation of artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please look at the other document, dated 8 June, called "order"? Will you please look at the document first? Is this order related in any way to the activities you engaged in related to logistics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This order is also related to the logistics agency -- before sending a unit to perform a particular task a logistic unit had to supply the unit with all the materiel and equipment, meals and other supplies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this order submitted to your agency as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this order was submitted to the logistics agency for the above-mentioned reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, were both of these orders signed in the customary way by the joint command, that is, both by the TO commander and the HVO commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were signed as shown on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you are a professional military man, Mr. Kevric, when does an order become an order that you have to comply with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me, an order is an order when it is signed by my commander. If he signs that order, then I can act on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, if a document, even it is called an "order", is signed by a person who is not your commander, or your superior, does it oblige you in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If an order is signed by someone else, it is not obligatory for me as an assistant commander of logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, did you also act in the way that you have just told us? In other words, did you act in 1992 only on the basis of orders by your authorised superiors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As an old soldier and familiar with the rules on the chain of command, that is how I always acted, and I think this is well known by everyone in Konjic, that I never did anything for which I was not ordered to act by my commander or about which I had not consulted him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kevric. These documents can now be returned to the files. Mr. Kevric, do you know that, for a time in 1992 -- that at some point in time the supreme command formed Tactical Groups, or, to be more precise, do you know whether a Tactical Group known as Tactical Group 1 was formed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know that Tactical Groups were formed and particularly Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason, Mr. Kevric, for the formation of Tactical Groups by the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason for the formation of Tactical Groups 1 and 2 was to lift the siege of the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Kevric, who was the first commander of Tactical Group 1 and where it was based?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of Tactical Group 1 was Mr. Mustafa Polutak, a former lieutenant-colonel in the former Yugoslav People's Army. Tactical Group 1 was based in Pazarici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the staff, you probably know and please will you tell the Trial Chamber if you do, whether, at some time early in June, a group of soldiers from Konjic was subordinated to the commander of the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning of June, the Gajret unit was subordinated to Tactical Group 1 which was sent from the town of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this the first group of soldiers leaving Konjic in the direction of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the first time that, from the municipal staff, a unit was going outside the area of responsibility of the municipal staff and was being placed under the command of another unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, in the staff, have certain problems, bearing in mind what you have told us so far, in providing the unit with the necessary uniforms, boots and everything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did have problems, as I have already said, because we were unprepared for the war and we had no reserves, and in order to equip those units with communications equipment, meals, cigarettes, we had to engage in preparations before sending this unit to Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was particularly active in carrying out this task assigned to him with regard to providing supplies and equipment for this unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Particularly active in this respect was Mr. Zejnil Delalic, who ensured communications equipment, quartermaster supplies, that is, uniforms, and cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before this group in Pazarici was subordinated to Mr. Polutak, did you, in the staff, talk about or reach any decisions on how this unit should be outfitted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Since this was the first time that a unit was being sent outside of the area of responsibility of the municipal TO command, we decided to make it a celebration and so members of the war presidency and members of the municipal staff and Mr. Zejnil Delalic was there together with members of the war presidency and TO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time of the send-off of these units, did Mr. Delalic have any command role in the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Zejnil Delalic had no command responsibility in the TO staff. He was there as a guest and he was shown special respect, because he was able to provide all this equipment and cigarettes, and we were honoured to have him as our guest.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, do you know who ordered the establishment of this unit, Gajret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the commander of the TO staff who ordered the establishment of the Gajret unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, were you personally present at this celebration when the unit was sent off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was personally present there and, after this official part and the parade, I went to Tarcin with the unit and with some officers. At Tarcin we stopped because of security reasons -- we could not go all the way to Pazaric. Subsequently, the unit was taken to Pazaric and then engaged in its task, which had to do with the lifting of the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in order to identify the send-off of this Gajret unit, I wanted to have the videotape shown where Mr. Kevric was also present, but knowing your position in relation to showing it again, I do not know if I should play it again, or maybe just continue with the rest of the questions without it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is not necessary -- it is not in dispute whether there was a send-off force or not. Does it matter if we play the tape? You can carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is precisely why I asked you, your Honours. I think the only controversy about it is that it relates to evidence according to which my client is a person of superior authority, but I do not need to belabour that, so I think that there is no controversy over the fact whether the witness was there. So, what I am going to do is I am going to limit myself to asking questions about his role in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am not going to try to show it again. Trust me, I do not wish to go into any kind of debate or argument over this. So, Mr. Kevric, can you please tell me, when a soldier addresses a superior officer, that is, in that period, how would the soldier address him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a soldier, when I would address my commander, I would address him as "Sir" and the rank, say "Major", or if there was no rank, then I had to tell him "Sir" or "Mr.", and say "Commander". So a soldier would also have to say, "Mr. Commander, soldier such and such needs such and such."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, if the person whom you are addressing has no military function, you do not need to address him with these titles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you a direct question. During this celebration when you were sending off these first units to Pazarici in order to be subordinated to Mr. Polutak, did Mr. Zejnil Delalic have any position of superiority, either military or civilian? You are a witness of these events.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Zejnil Delalic had no military or civilian function there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, do you know anything about the subsequent combat operations that were conducted by the staff of the Territorial Defence, or the joint command, or, more specifically, did you make any preparation in your command and in your staff for certain combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, since I was a member of the staff, we received an order from the TO staff of Bosnia to start preparations for combat operations in the direction of Borci and (INAUDIBLE).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the HVO initially take an active role in preparation of these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in our joint meetings, they were at first agreeing to joint combat operations. However, when we were supposed to go and start these operations, the HVO pulled out from this operation at Borci.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher to help me give the witness documents which we have already seen. They are in volume III of the supplement to the expert report of the military expert, and they are marked V-D/24 and V-D/25. I would like to ask certain questions. I am not going to ask again that these documents be admitted, since they have already been admitted before. (Handed). Could you first look at this document which is dated 12/6/92? Mr. Kevric, as a member of the TO staff, are you familiar with this order of this TO staff of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this order, because, as a member of the TO staff, I was involved in the preparation of this order, in its logistical aspects.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, when you received this order, did you start joint preparations for the operation which was to follow in Borci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we started the preparations for the aspect that was envisaged by the TO. We immediately requested additional equipment and food supplies so that the units would be completely ready when they go into combat. However, later, when the HVO pulled out from this operation, the TO staff found itself in a very difficult situation, because now it was virtually impossible to carry out this operation. So, we had an emergency mobilisation, but these new conscripts were not prepared and then the terrain in which these operations were to take place was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Kevric, I think you have provided enough details about what I wanted to address here. I would now like to ask you to look at the document dated 25 June 1992. It is addressed to the HVO staff, to the attention of Dinko Zebic. Mr. Kevric, since Mr. Dinko Zebic was the chief of staff in the joint command, can you tell me whether Dinko Zebic was personally involved in part of the preparation for this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dinko Zebic wanted to take part in this operation with his unit. However, this did not happen and I do not know the reason why the HVO did not take part in this operation, but he was the point person in the planning of this combat operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was this operation called -- what was its name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This operation's name was Oganj.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this document certain Tactical Groups are indicated. My first question to you, Mr. Kevric, is whether these Tactical Groups which are mentioned in this document have anything to do with the Tactical Groups established by the main staff of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the lifting of the siege of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These Tactical Groups really have nothing to do with Tactical Groups 1 and 2, which were established by the staff of the TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina. These are Tactical Groups that are at about 100 or 150 men strength and these were just in limited areas and they were just marked 1, 2, 3 and 4, to point to the particular areas. They have nothing to do with those Tactical Groups 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Kevric. Can you now tell me, after parting ways with the HVO, who issued the order for the combat Operation Oganj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The order for the Operation Oganj was issued by the commander of the TO Konjic, Mr. Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who was the commander of the Oganj Operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the Operation Oganj was Mr. Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- actually, let me ask you first, how long did this combat operation last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The combat operation Oganj lasted for about a month, or, more precisely, it started on 27 June and ended on 30 or 31 July.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the Operation Oganj, did a new commander of this operation arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a change took place, because Mr. Esad Ramic, the commander of this operation, was slightly wounded and Mr. Midhat Cerovac acted as commander of this operation and at that time he was chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, do you know whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic took part in this combat operation which had its codename Oganj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic, as coordinator, was given the task to be at Vranjske Stijene in order to coordinate with me. I was in the town of Konjic, or, more accurately, in the brewery, and we were to coordinate all units that were out in the field, because for this operation, we had several points where different units were placed and in order to facilitate the communication with me in Konjic and with Celebici, we had these several points.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, was at any time during the Operation Oganj, Mr. Zejnil Delalic become either the commander of this operation or any person of superior authority in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Delalic did not become a person of superior authority, nor did he take part in the combat operation, except in the sense that I have just indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric, let me now turn to some further questions on issues that you would have been familiar with as a member of the TO at that time. I would first like to talk to you about the development of the Territorial Defence in Konjic, that is, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the town itself. You have already testified to the document of 28 April in which you informed the staff of the supreme command about the persons who were already involved at that time. My question to you is: at the beginning, were there any officers of the former JNA in the TO staff, that is, the officers with previous experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning, when I first came to Konjic, there were three members of the former JNA. Those were Mr. Dinko Zebic, Hamza Janovic and Enver Redzepovic. They were former members of the Yugoslav People's Army, and, when they left it, they reported to the staff, and they were members of the staff before I arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony, you mentioned the assembly, that is, a session of the 17th April of 1992. Can you please tell me, war started after the declaration of independence. Did this State immediately pass certain laws that had to do with establishment of its armed forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a temporary instruction was adopted -- the former republican staff was renamed into the staff of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina; then the district staffs were established and the municipal staffs, which were established in municipalities. The municipal staff in Konjic, according to this provisional instruction, was subordinate directly to the BH TO staff, because the district staff in Mostar was not functional at the time, and this was the case until 17 November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, that means that you had the provisional instruction, which was issued by the TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina as early as April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, based on this instruction, the commander of the TO staff was no longer a member of war presidency -- he is subordinate directly to the staff of the TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether, during that period, that is, in April 1992, there was a mobilisation of the population and how was the Territorial Defence in Konjic organised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the decision of 17 April, a mobilisation took place, that is, units started being established and it depended on the settlements, or where there were small communities, platoons were formed and there was a detachment formed in Konjic. So, these units were later grouped, so companies were grouped into detachments and in Konjic there were about 12 detachments established in the end and then different branches were formed, which was an anti-aircraft company and artillery and then there was one platoon left, which was a platoon to Brdjani. Later platoons were established. The first attempt to establish a brigade in August failed, because of the combat operations, but later on the brigades were established -- in October and November the Suad Alic brigade was formed in Konjic and another one in, and then finally the 4th Corps was established and the municipal TO remains in place until January 1994; however, now, under the command under the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You very briefly but very graphically showed us the organisation and the development of Territorial Defence, that is, the units of the TO staff in Konjic. Can you tell me, in this development, from April until November, was there a phase during this development when there was a coordinator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could the Defence please repeat the question? I did not understand it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained to us how companies, platoons, detachments, battalions, brigades were established. My question to you now is: during the development of the army, was there a phase in which the role of coordinator was established in the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the army, there was no such phase in which there was a coordinator -- the role of coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, let us move to another area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think before you move into that area, we will have a break. When we come back, we will start in that area we are moving into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Will you please invite the witness to come in? I see two of you standing. What is it all about?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your permission, as you can see, my client, Mr. Mucic, is not in the courtroom. He has refused to come to the courtroom, because the Registry has prevented him from having contact with the investigator. At the same time, he has not waived his right to be present in the courtroom and for the hearing to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has waived his right to do that when he voluntarily and without any good reason stays away. I think he should be allowed to stay away until he decides to come back. We would not allow anybody's disobedience or rudeness to intimidate the Trial Chamber from doing the right thing. If he wants to stay away, he is free to do so. You may proceed, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, have you rested a little?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the break, I said that we would be moving on to another issue. Tell me, please, Mr. Kevric, do you know whether, in 1992, the war presidency was superior in relation to the TO staff of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war presidency of the municipality of Konjic was never superior to the TO staff of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But you have already covered that -- other witnesses have said that. How does it help to get the same statement repeated?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that the expert witness was the only one who spoke about that. This is a fact witness. An expert speaks on the basis of documents and this witness on the basis of personal knowledge, so I thought it was worth hearing it, and in view of the fact that in the folder of the expert witness there are two orders that could affect this witness, I would like those documents to be shown to the witness so we can hear his opinion. These are exhibits in the third volume of the documents attached to the expert report under V-A/12 and V-A/16. I have a sufficient number of copies for the Trial Chamber, for my colleagues and for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The first statement he made appeared to be conclusive as to whatever you want to say. He clearly stated that. At no stage could the war presidency be superior to the territorial group. If you want to compound it by going further, you could, but I think he said it all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, very briefly, so we can hear the view of the witness -- I will not tender this as exhibits, into evidence, but as these are documents from that time period and they may be familiar to the witness, perhaps it would be useful to hear him on them. Mr. Kevric, have you looked at these two documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were both documents issued by the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, both documents were issued by the war presidency and signed by the president of the war presidency of the municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As they are similar in content and both documents are orders, will you please look at the order that might have applied to your area of responsibility, saying that it is addressed to the rear agency, and requiring a certain kind of behaviour. Mr. Kevric, will you tell me -- let me first ask you whether you received this order from the war presidency at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I received this order from the war presidency. I am familiar with it. However, the same order does not apply to the rear body and the TO staff, because the war presidency cannot give orders to the TO staff. For me, this was just an information and nothing more -- without the permission or approval of my commander, I could not carry out this task.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all. Will these documents be returned to the files, please? Mr. Kevric, you have already told the court that you were appointed in April as assistant commander for logistics by the commander at the time, and then to the joint command by commander Boric and the chief of staff Zebic. In the course of the development of the army, as you described before the break, were new appointments made for the activities that you were responsible for in the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. After the small difference with the HVO because they did not participate in the Operation Oganj, the commander of the TO staff appointed me again assistant commander for logistics in the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could this document be marked for identification and shown to the witness, please? I have a sufficient number of copies for the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution and my colleagues. (Handed). Could you tell me the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D169/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric, have you looked at this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have looked at this document. It was signed by commander Ramic and it appoints me assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this one of the appointments you received in the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is one thing I am not able to understand. Mr. Kevric had the rank of a major and Mr. Ramic has the rank of a captain. How can a captain be ordering a major around?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps Colonel Kevric could explain this, because this was the first year of the war -- as we heard from generals and others, there were no ranks. There were just titles.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, your Honour, we cannot hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But there must be ranks within the TO. It was a military organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask Mr. Kevric. I am not very knowledgeable about such things. Maybe he can answer this question for you. Did you understand the question, Mr. Kevric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I fully understood the question and I shall try and answer it. Mr. Ramic Esad is an officer who completed the Academy of the Ground Forces for the infantry. Therefore, he is familiar -- he is more familiar with the planning of combat operations, he is familiar with weaponry. I am a logistics man and I could not be a unit commander. I could not be the commander of the TO staff and that is the reason why Mr. Ramic was appointed commander of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, in the course of 1992, were there, generally, ranks in the TO, or later the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and these ranks indicated here, were they the ranks that you had in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no ranks. There were duties by formations until 1994 when the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina established ranks -- until then, we only had duties such as commander, chief of staff -- the body for logistics, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I hope you are satisfied, your Honour, and as this is an appointment for Mr. Kevric issued on 3 August by the commander of the staff at the time, I think this document can be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may tender that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So Exhibit 169/1; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, do you know whether Zejnil Delalic, for a period of time in 1992, was appointed to any command military duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I do know that Mr. Zejnil Delalic was appointed commander of Tactical Group 1. I do not know the exact date, but as a staff officer -- that is assistant commander for logistics -- I was informed that at 2300 hours -- I was informed of that on 30 or 31 July.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How is it that you remember now when you were informed of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When taking over duty, when I moved to the joint command of the army of the federation, and also by looking through my notebook, I came across this note made in my notebook about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be possible for somebody to be appointed commander of a Tactical Group much earlier, without you being informed about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know that anyone was appointed commander of a Tactical Group from Konjic before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From that point in time, when, as you said, you learnt that Zejnil Delalic was appointed commander of Tactical Group 1, Mr. Kevric, was Mr. Zejnil Delalic from then on a person who was superior to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the moment I learnt that Mr. Zejnil Delalic was appointed commander of Tactical Group 1, he was never my superior commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Konjic was subordinated from that moment on to Mr. Delalic, or was Mr. Delalic the superior officer to your territorial staff in the municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipal staff of Konjic was never subordinated to Mr. Zejnil Delalic, nor was Mr. Zejnil Delalic ever a superior to the municipal staff. Mr. Zejnil Delalic was superior only to the unit that was sent to the Tactical Group from the TO staff of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Zejnil Delalic, after being appointed to this position, had any communication with the municipal staff of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that, because I was informed by the commander that there was communication in terms of the forwarding of orders, also a briefing about the HVO, because they had appropriated some equipment and --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, do you know what the Operation Jug is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I am familiar with that Operation Jug, because our units had to perform certain assignments, that is, the units that were sent to Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you well -- units from Konjic, during Operation South -- Jug -- were sent to Tactical Group 2 and not Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so, Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know where the combat operations were conducted in which units from Konjic participated within the framework of Operation Jug?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know, because I personally saw that unit off, and supplied it with resources, equipment, food and ammunition, and sent them to Tactical Group 2. I think that they were engaged in offensive operations around Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what duty or function was performed by Mr. Zejnil Delalic within the framework of the provisional command South -- Jug?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Mr. Zejnil Delalic, when the provisional command Jug was formed, he was appointed assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like this exhibit to be marked for identification and then shown to the witness. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D170/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am, because we received it in the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you assistant commander for logistics at that time in the municipal headquarters in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was assistant commander for logistics in the municipal staff of Konjic and our duty was to provide meals for our units, which were participating in combat operations, that is, in the Tactical Group. Actually, Tactical Groups 1 and 2, which both belonged to Operation Jug, because the operative group Jug did not have all the warehouses to keep the units supplied during combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Kevric, that even though Mr. Zejnil Delalic was a commander of the Tactical Group and in the provisional group Jug responsible for logistics, that he did not give you any orders in connection with these tasks, but only a request for providing a certain number of rations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It can be seen from this document that it is a request and not an order. If any other unit were to address me, for instance, a unit from Mostar could send a request from Prozor or from Sarajevo, if I had the required supplies, I could issue those supplies to that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were issuing the supplies, did you issue them based on the order of your own commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have already stated that no supplies could be issued without the signature of my commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since this is a document that is addressed specifically to the witness and is relevant in these proceedings, I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may tender it if you want to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the Defence Exhibit D170/1; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, let me move to another area now. Responding to my questions this morning, you stated that the Celebici barracks were taken over without fighting and that Mr. Delalic in Ovcari turned over the weapons that he found to you, since he was in charge of the transportation of these weapons. Can you tell me whether you know the location of the Celebici barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know the location of the Celebici barracks. It is located nine kilometres from the municipality of Konjic, to the left of the highway, about 150 to 200 metres away from the highway itself. It is surrounded by Paradzici, which is a Croatian village, and the Muslim village of Idbar, and across the Idbar River is the Serb village of Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know for which purposes the Celebici barracks were used after it was taken over and during this period of time of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know first the unit which took over the Celebici barracks was stationed there. These were mobile units, and they stayed there for about three to four days and they were stationed there -- they were accommodated there in order for them not to have to go to their homes, and then there was a storehouse for ammunition as well as later for food and other equipment. Then there was a prison, and a workshop for repair of weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did there come a time in 1992 when the special units of the Konjic MUP were also stationed in the Celebici barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that, in the beginning, I stated that there was a MUP unit, which was led by Miralem Musinovic, which was stationed there for a period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, did you have any contact with Celebici barracks with respect to your job and did you have any contacts with the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as contacts with the Celebici barracks is concerned, my job was to control issuance of the equipment in the warehouses that belonged to the TO Konjic. Later on, that included also the repair of weaponry, and the duty of the logistics staff was also feeding the prisoners, that is, the detainees who were in the prison. That is the quartermaster officer of the logistics staff was tasked with that duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, taking into consideration all these duties that you had to perform in the Celebici barracks issuing equipment and food and repair of weaponry, did you ever go to the Celebici barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did visit the barracks in different times -- I would issue different orders to the staff who were guarding and issuing this equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, we can say that you could tell the Trial Chamber what was the space -- the surface that this facility occupied -- was this a large facility, a medium sized or a small sized facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. Is this a facility that was used by the TO, or the entire barracks?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, the entire compound, was this large, medium or a small sized facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The barracks compound is rather large. There are two parts -- the near part and the far part. There is the administration building, then, since it was used for fuel, it had those facilities. In the upper part -- the far end -- there were three or four fuel storages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you went to the warehouses where ammunition and equipment were kept, which way did you use to get there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I went to visit the warehouses, from the gate I would go directly to the warehouse on the upper road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please take the pointer and, if you can, show to the Trial Chamber -- if you can recognise it in this model, show us how you went to the ammunition warehouse. You can just extend it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So, this is the gate and I would take this road (witness indicates) and then I would come up here -- there are some letters here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In order for us all to be able to hear what you have just said, could you step up to the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot do it from here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you take this upper road -- Mr. Kevric, were you in a situation to see the structures that are in a lower end of the compound and, also, were you able to see what was going on there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you enter, you sort of bear to the right, and you only see the roofs of these structures, and they are closed -- there are windows there, which were sort of darkened -- how shall I put it -- they had darkened glass, so you could not see through them. On the way back, it was the same case -- I would take the same road back. It was only if somebody was standing around these buildings that you could see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to play a portion of the tape of the drive through the facility. It has been tendered before, but I would like to play it for the witness again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose we could all travel to Celebici to see how we could go into that place. I think that might be a more successful way of doing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would not mind suggesting that, if we could set up a hearing there. Could you please play this excerpt number 2, and without audio, please. May I ask the technical booth to play excerpt number 2, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kevric, you probably recognised the facility through which this vehicle drove. Can you just state for the Trial Chamber what facility this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the compound of the Celebici barracks. This was the lower part without the fuel depots.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you talked about the structures on the upper part, did your visits to the Celebici camps -- or, in order not to make it a leading question, what was the objective of your visits to the Celebici barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The objective of my visits was exclusively the control of the staff who worked in the warehouse of the military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We saw a large number of trucks in this video. Can you tell me, are these the trucks on which this military materiel was normally brought into the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This large number of trucks, which happened to be there -- that was a large convoy, which brought in a lot of military equipment and other equipment and food. When any of this equipment was issued to any of the units, and there were 12 of them all together, for each of these units, two or three truck loads would be sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kevric, you said that you were also in charge of the preparation of meals. Can you tell me, which service within your staff was in charge of food preparation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the logistics staff, it was the task of the quartermaster service to prepare food.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you prepare meals for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We prepared meals for the TO units, we would prepare them for the MUP units, we would prepare them for the Igman company, we would prepare them for the prisoners, and we would prepare them for some refugees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were these meals prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The meals were prepared first in a single location -- that was in the Igman company -- and that was because of the shelling which damaged gas installations, and also in Sipad which was the forestry company.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the court what were the supplies of basic food stocks in Konjic in 1992 and what did you have at your disposal in order to carry out this task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally, as an assistant commander for logistics, I do not recall a more difficult period than the one between April and August of 1992. The population was not prepared for the war. The TO staff had no reserves. There was just not enough food around. There were only some larger supplies of sugar at that time in Konjic, but as far as flour, meat, meat products, fresh vegetables, spices -- we had none of that, so we really had enormous problems in preparation of meals. We could not give breakfast to either refugees, soldiers, workers or detainees, or anything but soup, which consisted of just rice and oil. The situation changed a little bit later on when we received a shipment of flour. The food which was prepared in our kitchens was such as it could be at the time. We all ate the same food, starting from me, who was in charge of the logistics, down to the soldiers and to the detainees in Celebici. The biggest problems we faced was that, in the month of April, we found no containers for transportation of these meals, or any containers from which these refugees or detainees could eat. We had practically nothing. In the way of an example, let me tell you: since we did not have anything to give to soldiers to eat for breakfast except for some canned food occasionally, we had to, in early fall, make some plum jam. We had a certain amount of sugar so we distributed it around villages for people to make jam and this is what was then distributed around.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you now mentioned the fall of 1992, can you tell the Trial Chamber whether Konjic is known as a region -- as a plum-growing region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Konjic is indeed known for plum production, especially the left bank of the Neretva River valley.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you mentioned it, I am familiar with the Turkish local word for jam, which was "bestilj", so can you tell us what you were called at the end of the year by citizens of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a joke -- we were called "Alija's bestiljani", because they knew we had nothing else to give to people, to soldiers but plum jam for breakfast.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you basically cooked the food in a single location. At first it was one, then there were two locations. Was this food identical in quality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The food was identical, that is, the recipes were the same, even though they were stretched, they were cooked in the same cauldrons and they were in the same pots and they were transported in the same containers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, were all people to whom these meals -- for whom these meals were prepared, were all these people given the same rations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were all given the same rations based on the number of people that were put on these lists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have another area of questioning for this witness, but it is 5.30 now. So maybe it would be good for the witness to get a break from this long questioning of today and maybe we, too, could benefit from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think you might continue tomorrow morning at 10.00 a.m. The Trial Chamber will now rise. (At 5.30 p.m. the matter adjourned until Thursday, 16 April 1998, at 10.00 a.m.) 23 24 25
